info.name: Kong Wrapper - Analytics & Monitoring
info.description:
Konnect monitoring and analytics through the kong-wrapper service.

## Before you run

Set one collection variable:

- `baseUrl` - `http://localhost:3000` for local, or `https://forgesphere.probestack.io/kong-wrapper` for the deployed service.

That is enough. Run the collection top to bottom and `00. Setup` works the rest out: it picks the first stored profile, derives that profile's region from its admin URL, and captures a control plane, its name, and a gateway service for the requests that follow.

Override any of it by setting `profileId`, `controlPlaneId`, `controlPlaneName` or `serviceId` by hand - anything already set is left alone.

Do **not** set a region. It is derived into `profileRegion` from the chosen profile. A region that disagrees with the profile makes Konnect answer with an empty control plane list and a 200, which looks like an empty org rather than a mistake, and then every request after it fails on a blank id.

`patToken` is only needed on a fresh install with no stored profile. `Verify and store Konnect PAT` skips itself when a profile is already selected, and that request is the one that writes a PAT, in plain text, into the `kong_config` collection.

Requests that need a captured id skip themselves with a reason when it is missing, rather than sending a blank id and returning a 404 that reads like a broken endpoint.

## Start with the Dashboard request

`GET /analytics/dashboard` is the one a frontend should call. **`profileId` is its only required parameter.** The wrapper resolves the control plane, infers the region, defaults the window to 24H, then fetches the analytics query, the services list, the routes list and data plane health in parallel and returns them as one response - with route and service **names** already joined in, so nothing is left for the client to look up.

The requests under it are the underlying, Konnect-shaped endpoints. They are still useful for drill-down and for scoping a roll-up to a single entity, but a screen should not have to assemble itself out of them.

## Reading the results

Tests assert the things that can silently go wrong, not just status codes:

- Entity ids must come back bare, with the `{control_plane_id}:{entity_id}` composite kept alongside. Filtering Konnect by a bare id matches nothing and does not error.
- `time series sums to totals` fails precisely when Konnect renames `request_start`.
- `status codes were parsed` fails when the status field moves. It reads `response_http_status` (a string), while the *filter* field is `status_code` - Konnect uses different names on each side, and getting it wrong reports a 0% error rate rather than failing.
- On the dashboard, `names resolved` fails if the services or routes lookup did not land, which is the difference between a genuinely unnamed entity and a broken join.

An empty result is not a failure. Konnect retains 14 days, lags roughly 50 seconds behind live traffic, and the control plane may simply be idle. The console logs the record count and, in `Raw requests`, the field names of the first record, so you can tell the two apart.

Entities deleted inside the retention window still have traffic. Their rows are kept and flagged `deleted: true` with a null name, so the tables still reconcile with the totals.

request.description:
One call for a whole monitoring screen. **Only `profileId` is required.**

The wrapper resolves the control plane (when the profile has exactly one), infers the region from the profile's stored admin URL, defaults the window to 24H, then fans out to Konnect in parallel - the analytics query, the services list, the routes list and data plane health - joins the composite `{control_plane_id}:{entity_id}` ids against the bare config ids, and returns once.

So `topRoutes` arrives as `{ name, paths, service: { name } , requests, errorRatePercent, p95LatencyMs }` rather than a UUID the client has to look up. Nothing is left to join.

Disabled params, all optional:
- `controlPlaneId` / `controlPlaneName` - required only when the profile has more than one control plane; the error names the candidates.
- `timeRange` - defaults to 24H here (the raw endpoints default to 1H).
- `include` - trim the payload to the sections a screen actually renders.
- `region` - inferred from the profile; sending it still overrides.

Entities deleted inside the 14 day analytics window keep their traffic rows, flagged `deleted: true` with a null name, so the table still reconciles with the totals.

request.description:
The main dashboard call. Server-side roll-up over raw Konnect records: totals, error rate, latency percentiles, status histograms, top routes/services/consumers and a gap-filled time series.

`timeRange` accepts `15M`, `1H`, `6H`, `12H`, `24H`, `7D`.

Disabled query params worth enabling:
- `excludeUnmatched=false` - include requests that matched no route. These are internet scanner probes that 404, excluded by default so an idle gateway does not report a permanent error rate.
- `maxRecords` - raise it if `meta.truncated` is true.
- `topN` - how many entries in each top list.

request.description:
Data plane node status plus the config hash the control plane expects. Comparing the two is the direct way to confirm a decK apply actually reached the gateways rather than just the control plane.

If only one of the two upstream calls fails the response degrades and reports it inline. If both fail the error propagates, so this never reports a healthy-looking control plane when it could not reach Konnect at all.
